title: Promotion rollback can delete the existing catalog and manifest
reasoning: Rollback deletes existing destinations based on whether they existed before promotion, rather than whether they were successfully backed up or replaced. If the first catalog rename fails, rollback can delete the original catalog without a backup. If installing the staged catalog fails after the catalog backup succeeds, rollback restores the catalog but deletes the untouched original manifest because its backup has not yet been created.
reproduction: Start with an installed catalog and manifest. Inject an OSError into staged_catalog.replace(catalog_root). After rollback, the old catalog is restored but its manifest is deleted.
recommendation: Track completed promotion operations explicitly and undo only those operations. Never delete an original destination whose backup was not successfully created.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing preservation test rejects an invalid archive before promotion begins; it does not exercise failures during any rename.
suggestedRegressionTest: Extend installation-preservation coverage with failures at each promotion rename and assert the original catalog and manifest remain byte-for-byte intact.
